meta.title: Postpartum Doula Certification
meta.description: How to earn the ADA Postpartum Doula credential: an ADA-approved training program, the written and practical exam, fees, results and renewal.

hero.title: ADA Postpartum Doula
hero.line: For doulas who blend traditional Asian postpartum practices with modern, evidence-based care.
hero.imageAlt: A trainee changes a training doll’s diaper during an ADA Postpartum Doula Program session

steps.title: How to get certified
steps.intro: The ADA credential for postpartum and newborn care. Five steps take you from an ADA-approved program to a public record in the ADA registry.

s1.title: Complete an ADA-approved training program
s1.body: {count} modules, usually {days} days of intensive instruction, in person or online. American Red Cross Infant CPR is included. Training fees vary by provider. Find an ADA course

s2.title: Register for an exam date
s2.bodyNext: The next exam is on {date}. The exam fee is {fee}, paid to ADA. Your training provider guides you through registration, or you can contact ADA. Exam dates
s2.bodyNone: Exam sessions are scheduled after each training cohort. The exam fee is {fee}, paid to ADA. Your training provider guides you through registration, or you can contact ADA. Exam dates

s3.title: Sit the written and practical exams
s3.body: Exams are held at {location}: a {written}-minute written exam and a {practical}-minute one-on-one practical exam. Bring a valid government-issued photo ID. Exam day and ID

s4.title: Get your result
s4.body: By email in about {days} business days. The pass mark is {pass}/{max}. A certified ADA examiner assesses the practical exam.

s5.title: Join the registry, then renew
s5.body: ADA issues your certificate, numbered in the form {format}, and lists you in the ADA registry. The certificate is valid for {validity}, and renewal costs {fee}. Check the registry

exam.title: What’s on the exam
exam.intro: The exam covers the {count} modules of the program. The written exam asks multiple-choice and short-answer questions. The practical exam is a hands-on demonstration of doula skills, one-on-one with an examiner.
exam.imageAlt: An instructor teaches a session of the ADA Postpartum Doula Program, with a slide on a wall screen
exam.caption: An instructor teaches a session of the ADA Postpartum Doula Program. {date}.

postpartumRecovery.title: Postpartum Recovery
postpartumRecovery.description: Stages of body recovery, wound care assessment, vital-sign monitoring, and traditional recovery principles such as warming and circulation support.

newbornCare.title: Newborn Care
newbornCare.description: Bottle and breast feeding technique, bathing and umbilical care, evidence-based safe sleep, soothing, and milestone tracking.

breastfeedingSupport.title: Breastfeeding Support
breastfeedingSupport.description: Latch and positioning, engorgement, low supply and nipple pain, pumping, and when to refer to a lactation consultant.

culturalTraditions.title: Cultural Traditions
culturalTraditions.description: Chinese zuo yuezi (<zh>坐月子</zh>), Korean sanhujori (<ko>산후조리</ko>) and Japanese satogaeri (<ja>里帰り</ja>), along with confinement meals and family dynamics.

nutrition.title: Nutrition & Meal Planning
nutrition.description: Postpartum recipes across Asian traditions, and dietary guidance for breastfeeding.

emotionalWellness.title: Emotional Wellness
emotionalWellness.description: Recognizing postpartum depression and anxiety, active listening, cultural stigma, boundaries and referral protocols.

safetyEmergency.title: Safety & Emergency
safetyEmergency.description: Infant CPR (American Red Cross), choking response, emergency protocols, safe-sleep setup, and when to call emergency services and when to call the pediatrician.

fees.title: Fees and renewal
fees.caption: ADA Postpartum Doula fees and renewal

exam.label: Exam registration
exam.note: Paid to ADA. Covers the written and the practical exam.

retake.label: Retake
retake.note: For each new attempt after a result below {pass}/{max}, at least {days} days after your last attempt.

renewal.label: Renewal
renewal.note: {years, plural, one {Every year} other {Every # years}}, to keep your certificate current.

tuition.label: Program tuition
tuition.note: Paid to the training program, not to ADA. Some scholarship funding may be available. <link>Scholarships</link>

fees.footnote: Exam fees are paid to ADA. Training fees are paid to the training program.

cta.noDate: Exam sessions are scheduled after each training cohort.

links.renew: Renew {years, plural, one {every year} other {every # years}} to keep your certificate current.

experience.a: No. No prior doula experience is required. ADA-approved training programs take you from beginner to exam-ready.

register.q: How do I register for the exam?
register.a: After you complete an ADA-approved training program, your training provider guides you through registration. You can also contact ADA at <mail>{email}</mail> or <tel>{phone}</tel>.

retake.a: You can retake the exam for {fee}, at least {days} days after your attempt. Review the areas to improve with your training program before you retake.

languages.a: Training and exams are offered in {languages}. Choose your exam language when you register. All exam materials, including instructions and questions, are then in that language.

afterPass.a: ADA issues your certification, valid for {validity}, and lists you in the ADA registry. Insurance providers can verify your certification there.
